newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat comes to life on dry weather nerves.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat comes to life on dry weather nerves.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures came to life on Wednesday in a rising market as jitters began to strike over dry conditions in Australia's south-east areas.
A total of 38 lots traded, breaking the drought of nil or negligible trades in the dormant market of recent weeks.

The two nearest-term contracts both rose well on Wednesday, with May 1997 up by A$3.00 to A$184.00 a tonne and July 1997 up A$4.50 to A$185.50 in sales on the SFE floor. January 1998 slipped by A$1.50 to A$172.00 in a single trade.
Settlement prices also rose well across the contract range, generally by between A$2.00 and A$5.00 a tonne. The most heavily-traded contract, July 1997, rose by A$5.50 while May 1997 rose by A$2.50.

Wednesday's trading floor activity followed a more active overnight market on the SFE's SYCOM system when six trades went through at higher prices in November 1997 and January 1998. It also followed Chicago's rise on weather concerns.
Graham Smith of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said dry weather in southern New South Wales and Victoria had led to strong buying for feed grains, especially from Victoria.
Some short covering emerged on the SFE market, he said.

"Finally people are deciding they had better take some cover in these markets. There is concern about shortness of supply in the near months of May and July (and expectations) that the market will firm up considerably over the next few weeks.
"It's all pressured by feed grain buying out of Victoria. They are a little bit nervous about the late break in the weather," he said.
